title: Proactive compatibility probing and fallback planes for multi-variant deploys
creator: Asha Kapoor
summary: Implement a proactive compatibility probing layer and explicit 'fallback planes' that separate spillover, regional failover, and degraded-mode lanes for multi-variant model deploys. The goal is to reduce blind spillovers and unexpected semantic regressions during canaries and A/B tests while preserving low-latency paths for tiered capacity customers.
background: Current rollout behavior relies on reactive signals (latency/error spikes) and coarse capacity thresholds. That leads to noisy spillover, cross-tenant impact when regional nodes hit limits, and cases where incompatible variants degrade user-facing semantics before rollbacks trigger. We need an intermediate probing/compatibility phase that validates routing decisions per-tenant and per-region before we ramp traffic, plus separate fallback planes (fast-evict, regional-queue, degraded-quality) to control how traffic moves under pressure.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New probing API can submit synthetic probes against a candidate variant and return compatibility metrics within 3s. 2) Fallback planes are configurable per-deployment and enforceable by the runtime router. 3) Canary ramps use probes to allocate initial 0.5-5% traffic with fail-open/close thresholds. 4) Rollback automation triggers if semantic divergence > configured threshold (PR-based evals) or latency SLO breaches persist for X minutes. 5) Unit and integration tests for routing changes with simulated region outages.
design_notes:
- Introduce a 'probe profile' attached to a rollout (seed prompts, expected tokens distribution, metric hooks).
- Probes run from the target region and a cross-region shadow to detect compatibility and region-specific degradations.
- Define three fallback planes: FAST_EVICT (immediate drop to variant fallback), REGIONAL_QUEUE (spill to local regional pool with degraded latency but preserved availability), and QUALITY_DEGRADE (route to quantized/cheaper variant).
- Router policy composition: ProbeResult -> AdmissionScore -> FallbackPlane selection -> TrafficSlice. AdmissionScore factors include semantic-match, tail-latency, KV-cache hit rate, and tenant-priority.
- Provide dry-run mode where probes influence but do not re-route production traffic for 24h.
implementation_plan:
1) Spike: probe harness and shape of probe payloads (2d). 2) Runtime: add probe scheduler and per-variant probe state (5d). 3) Router: implement fallback-plane policy engine and admission scoring (4d). 4) Console: UI to attach probe profiles to rollouts and visualize probe heatmaps (3d). 5) QA and staged rollout (4d).
Deliverables: probe harness library, router policy config schema, console probe UI, integration test suite, runbook for operators.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for probe scheduler, admission scoring, and fallback selection.
- Integration tests simulating: a) region outage while canary at 5% b) semantic drift detected in probes c) KV cache warm vs cold differences.
- E2E staging with synthetic tenants and load generator; assert no cross-tenant SLA violations and correct fallback plane selection.
- Add regression tests to CI ensuring admission score changes are deterministic given probe inputs.
monitoring_and_alerts:
- Probe health dashboard (latency, success rate, semantic score distribution).
- Alert: Probe failure rate > 5% for 10min.
- Alert: Fallback-plane activations > threshold (per-region) -> page on-call.
- New tracing span 'probe.evaluation' with tags: variant, region, tenant, semantic-score.
- Post-mortem template updated to attribute incidents to probe vs runtime failures.
rollout_steps: 1) Merge probe harness and basic probe scheduling behind feature flag. 2) Run probes in dry-run on internal canaries for 48h. 3) Enable fallback planes for non-critical tenants (low customer impact) and observe for 1 week. 4) Gradually enable for all canaries and add automated rollback signatures. 5) Post-launch: 30-day monitoring review and iterate thresholds.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Probe false positives cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require multi-signal consensus (semantic+latency+error) before automated rollback; initial rollback actions limited to non-critical tenants.
Risk: Added probe traffic increases cost. Mitigation: sample probes and cap probe rate per deployment.
Risk: Complexity in router policy leads to regressions. Mitigation: strict schema validation, canary of router changes, and a rollback plan for router binaries.

2026-03-06: UX sync: console will show a probe heatmap and an action to 'promote' probe results into an admission override for core tenants. Need mockups. - Priya (PM)

2026-03-09: First integration test run: semantic scores correlated with telemetry; found a false-positive case when KV cache cold start simulated — adjusted scoring weight to discount short-lived latency spikes. - QA
